lead: At the limit state of collapse in flexure, the compressive stress in the concrete is not uniform: it follows the design stress–strain curve, a parabola and then a flat top at 0.446fck. Integrating that shape over the compression depth gives two numbers, the stress block parameters: the total force C = 0.36fck b xu and its position, 0.42xu below the top. With them a beam's moment of resistance is one force times one lever arm. Only a few universities derive the parameters in their own right; most use them directly in beam design.
prereq: You need: the concrete and steel design curves in properties of concrete and reinforcing steel and 0.446fck and 0.87fy from partial safety factors.

blocks.text: IS 456 analyses a section at collapse in flexure with these assumptions: plane sections remain plane; the strain in the extreme compression fibre is 0.0035; the tensile strength of concrete is ignored; the stress in concrete follows the design curve (parabola to a strain of 0.002, then flat at 0.446f<sub>ck</sub>); and the strain in the tension steel at failure is not less than f<sub>y</sub>/(1.15E<sub>s</sub>) + 0.002, that is 0.87f<sub>y</sub>/Es + 0.002.

Let x<sub>u</sub> be the depth of the neutral axis at collapse. Strain is zero there and 0.0035 at the top, so the strain is 0.002 at a height of (0.002/0.0035) x<sub>u</sub> = 4/7 x<sub>u</sub> above the neutral axis, that is 3/7 x<sub>u</sub> = 0.429x<sub>u</sub> below the top. Above that level the concrete stress is the flat 0.446f<sub>ck</sub>; below it the stress is a parabola that falls to zero at the neutral axis.
Per unit width, the compression force is the area of the stress diagram, written in terms of the peak stress 0.446f<sub>ck</sub>:

rectangle: (3/7) x<sub>u</sub> × 0.446f<sub>ck</sub>;  parabola: (2/3) × (4/7) x<sub>u</sub> × 0.446f<sub>ck</sub>
total: (3/7 + 8/21) × 0.446f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub> = (17/21) × 0.446f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub> = 0.361f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub> ≈ 0.36f<sub>ck</sub> x<sub>u</sub>
blocks.where: The parabola's area is two-thirds of the rectangle that encloses it.

blocks.text: The centroid of the rectangle is (3/14) x<sub>u</sub> below the top. The centroid of the parabolic part is 3/8 of its depth below its flat (vertex) end, that is 3/7 x<sub>u</sub> + (3/8)(4/7) x<sub>u</sub> = (9/14) x<sub>u</sub> below the top. Taking moments about the top:

blocks.where: So C = 0.36f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> acts at 0.42x<sub>u</sub> below the top, and the lever arm to the steel is z = d − 0.42x<sub>u</sub>.

blocks.text: The stress block is therefore not a uniform stress of 0.36f<sub>ck</sub>; 0.36f<sub>ck</sub> is the stress the force would have if it were spread evenly over x<sub>u</sub>, and 0.42 locates where it really acts. Equilibrium (C = T) and moments give
0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>,   M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>)
blocks.where: b and d in mm, A<sub>st</sub> in mm², f<sub>ck</sub> and f<sub>y</sub> in N/mm²; M<sub>u</sub> in N mm. Eliminating x<sub>u</sub> gives the IS 456 form M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> d (1 − A<sub>st</sub> f<sub>y</sub>/(b d f<sub>ck</sub>)).

sections.h3: Limiting neutral axis depth and limiting moment

blocks.text: For a ductile failure the steel must reach 0.87f<sub>y</sub> before the concrete crushes, so its strain must be at least 0.87f<sub>y</sub>/Es + 0.002 when the top fibre is at 0.0035. From similar triangles, x<sub>u,max</sub>/d = 0.0035/(0.0035 + 0.87f<sub>y</sub>/Es + 0.002):

The last column is 0.36 (x<sub>u,max</sub>/d)(1 − 0.42 x<sub>u,max</sub>/d): for Fe415, 0.36 × 0.48 × (1 − 0.42 × 0.48) = 0.138. A section with x<sub>u</sub> < x<sub>u,max</sub> is under-reinforced (steel yields first, ductile); x<sub>u</sub> = x<sub>u,max</sub> is the limiting (balanced) section; IS 456 does not allow x<sub>u</sub> > x<sub>u,max</sub>, which would be over-reinforced and fail suddenly by crushing. SP 16 tabulates these constants for every grade.

examples.question: A singly reinforced beam is 230 mm wide with an effective depth of 450 mm and has 3 bars of 16 mm of Fe415 in M25 concrete. Find x<sub>u</sub>, check whether it is under-reinforced, and find its moment of resistance M<sub>u</sub>.
steps: x<sub>u,max</sub> = 0.48 × 450 = 216 mm. Since 105.2 < 216 the section is under-reinforced.
Concrete force C = 0.36 × 25 × 230 × 105.2 = 217,800 N, equal to T (check).
examples.answer: x<sub>u</sub> = 105.2 mm < 216 mm, under-reinforced; M<sub>u</sub> ≈ 88.4 kNm.

examples.question: For the same beam (230 mm × 450 mm effective, M25, Fe415), find the limiting moment of resistance M<sub>u,lim</sub> and the steel area that produces it.
steps: x<sub>u,max</sub> = 0.48 × 450 = 216 mm, the limit for Fe415 from the table.
A<sub>st,lim</sub> = C/(0.87f<sub>y</sub>) = 447,120/361.05 = 1238 mm². More steel than this would push x<sub>u</sub> past 216 mm.
examples.answer: M<sub>u,lim</sub> ≈ 160.6 kNm with A<sub>st,lim</sub> ≈ 1238 mm²; the beam of the first worked example, at 88.4 kNm, uses a little over half of it.

traps: The force is 0.36f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub>, not 0.446f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub>: 0.446f<sub>ck</sub> is the peak stress of the block, and using it as the average overstates C by about 24 %.
The lever arm is d − 0.42x<sub>u</sub>, not d − 0.42d and not d − x<sub>u</sub>/3 (the WSM value).

Steel strain at 0.87f<sub>y</sub> for HYSD bars is 0.87f<sub>y</sub>/Es + 0.002 (0.0038 for Fe415). Leaving out the 0.002 gives x<sub>u,max</sub>/d = 0.66 for Fe415, which allows over-reinforced, brittle sections.
Do not divide 0.36 or 0.87 by another partial safety factor; both already include γ<sub>m</sub>.

If the computed x<sub>u</sub> exceeds x<sub>u,max</sub>, the singly reinforced formula M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>(d − 0.42x<sub>u</sub>) no longer holds; redesign the section or add compression steel.

quiz.q: State the IS 456 stress block parameters for flexure.
quiz.a: Compression force 0.36f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> acting at 0.42x<sub>u</sub> below the extreme compression fibre.

quiz.q: State x<sub>u,max</sub>/d for Fe250, Fe415 and Fe500.
Why does the strain 0.002 occur at 3/7 of x<sub>u</sub> below the top?
quiz.a: Strain varies linearly from 0.0035 at the top to zero at the neutral axis, so 0.002 occurs at 0.002/0.0035 = 4/7 of x<sub>u</sub> above the neutral axis, which is 3/7 of x<sub>u</sub> below the top.

quiz.q: For f<sub>ck</sub> = 30 N/mm², b = 300 mm and x<sub>u</sub> = 120 mm, find C.
Find M<sub>u,lim</sub> for a 250 mm × 500 mm (effective) beam in M20 with Fe500.
Why does Fe500 have a smaller x<sub>u,max</sub>/d than Fe415?
quiz.a: Fe500 needs a larger strain (0.0042 against 0.0038) to reach its design stress, so the neutral axis must sit higher for the steel to be stretched that far when the top reaches 0.0035.

quiz.q: A student finds x<sub>u</sub> = 240 mm for a Fe415 beam with d = 450 mm. What does that mean, and what should be done?
quiz.a: x<sub>u</sub>/d = 0.53 > 0.48: the section is over-reinforced and would fail by crushing before the steel yields. IS 456 does not allow it; increase the depth or width, or design it as doubly reinforced.

beyond: For high-strength concrete the flat top and the ultimate strain 0.0035 no longer hold, and newer codes reduce the stress block parameters as f<sub>ck</sub> rises. ACI 318 uses an equivalent rectangle of 0.85f'c over a depth β₁c instead, and Eurocode 2 uses 0.8x at the design strength; all three give nearly the same M<sub>u</sub> for ordinary concretes. Search next for "Whitney rectangular stress block", "Eurocode 2 rectangular stress block" and "strain compatibility method".

figure.caption: The beam of the first worked example at collapse. Strain is a straight line from 0.0035 at the top to the steel, which is far past its yield strain of 0.0038. The stress block is flat at 0.446f<sub>ck</sub> down to 3/7 of x<sub>u</sub> and a parabola below; its force 217.8 kN acts 0.42x<sub>u</sub> from the top and balances the steel force.
